key: Right wouldest Thou be, O LORD, were I to contend with Thee, yet will I reason with Thee: Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper? Wherefore are all they secure that deal very treacherously?
s: Opening a chapter in which even his own kin betray him, the prophet puts a question to the LORD; Rashi, on 12:1, reads him as knowing God will be right, yet arguing so that God will make His way known to him.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Jeremiah 12:1, at [411,1]). Plain sense faithful: the chapter opens on the prophet’s question to the LORD, and 12:6 tells him his brethren and his father’s house have dealt treacherously with him; no four-word repeat of the key. Rashi on 12:1 says that when he argues he knows God will be right, yet he wishes to reason with Him so that God will make His way known to him: the reading is his, without drift. Radak and Metzudat David read the opening the same way. Entry passes entry-check unchanged.
